deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
The production fix is inherited (ModelAclGraphManager.capture calls super().capture and AscendModelState overrides dummy_inputs_embeds with the compatible signature), so no mandatory runtime code change is needed. Work is verification/tests and guarding Ascend-specific assumptions:
1) vllm_ascend/worker/v2/aclgraph_utils.py::ModelAclGraphManager.capture: after updating the vLLM pin, confirm it still just wraps the model in ModelWithContext and delegates. The new upstream code calls requires_raw_input_tokens(model) on the wrapped object; ModelWithContext.__getattr__ already falls back to original_model, but add/adjust a test that asserts this (otherwise raw-token models such as deepseek_v4/deepseek_v41 VL would incorrectly get input_ids=None).
2) vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_states/default.py::AscendModelState: keep prepare_dummy_inputs limited to positions + engram dummy inputs (do NOT re-add inputs_embeds there; the base capture now supplies it). Ensure dummy_inputs_embeds(num_tokens, input_ids=None) remains the only place doing the fine-grained embedding-TP dummy exchange and returns encoder_runner.inputs_embeds / self.inputs_embeds. Note upstream now calls it only on the first PP rank when supports_multimodal_inputs or enable_prompt_embeds is set.
3) AscendQwen4ExpModelState.prepare_dummy_inputs and EngramModelState.prepare_dummy_inputs must rely on the base capture for inputs_embeds and only add their model-specific keys (query_start_loc/ngram_context/engram_*); remove any local assumption that super() returns inputs_embeds.
4) Audit Ascend multimodal models for the new input_ids=None behavior: deepseek_v4/vl_model.py and deepseek_v41/vl_model.py already set requires_raw_input_tokens=True and stay unchanged; minimax_m3_vl and kimi_k3 dspark consume inputs_embeds when present. Any Ascend MM wrapper whose forward reads input_ids even when inputs_embeds is provided must set requires_raw_input_tokens=True.
5) Update/add UTs in tests/ut/worker/v2/test_aclgraph.py (and tests around model_states) mirroring upstream test_capture_inputs_match_execute_model: parameterize supports_multimodal_inputs/enable_prompt_embeds x requires_raw_input_tokens x first/non-first PP and assert input_ids is None when inputs_embeds replaces it, inputs_embeds is not None, dummy_inputs_embeds is invoked exactly once on the first PP rank, and prepare_dummy_inputs still returns only positions/engram keys. Add a prompt-embeds FULL/PIECEWISE (and breakable VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH) replay test analogous to upstream test_breakable_cudagraph_inputs_embeds_debug_replay.
deep_analysis.risk: Low-to-medium. Because vllm-ascend inherits the captured-input selection, the main regression risk is a capture/execute_model mismatch for Ascend multimodal or prompt-embeds models in FULL/PIECEWISE ACL graph replay: a model that still requires raw input_ids without declaring requires_raw_input_tokens will now receive input_ids=None and may error or produce wrong results. The ModelWithContext wrapper must keep the requires_raw_input_tokens attribute reachable. deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This is a hard API break, not just a test migration. First blocker: vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning.may_override_num_blocks is deleted, but vllm-ascend imports it at module scope in vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_config_builder.py:20, models/kimi_k3/paired_sfa_cache.py:16, models/glm5next/cache_config.py:21, models/qwen4_exp/cache_config.py:18-20 (the kv_cache_utils fallback also no longer has it), models/deepseek_v41/cache_config.py:12, models/step5/cache_config.py:46, and quantization/methods/kv_cache/turboquant/cache.py:16. These imports raise ImportError before any NPU startup. Remove them and stop applying the override inside Ascend planners: upstream get_kv_cache_configs still applies num_gpu_blocks_override before calling the builder, and it now passes the already-overridden/auto-fitted/min-rank num_blocks. Treat the num_blocks argument as authoritative.

Second blocker: get_kv_cache_config_from_groups changed from available_memory: int to num_blocks: int. In vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_config_builder.py, get_ascend_kv_cache_config_from_groups still takes available_memory and, at lines 544 and 564, calls _upstream_get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(vllm_config, pool, pool_size) and (vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, available_memory) with byte counts; post-commit these are interpreted as block counts and will allocate/plan absurd block numbers. Change both calls to pass the actual num_blocks. Best approach: make get_ascend_kv_cache_config_from_groups take num_blocks (not available_memory), thread it into get_qwen4_exp_kv_cache_config, paired_sfa_cache_config, get_step5_kv_cache_config_from_groups, get_deepseek_v41_kv_cache_config, get_glm5_next_kv_cache_config, tq_cache.cache_config and _get_kv_cache_config_deepseek_v4_main, and drop the internal may_override + memory\u2192blocks division in those helpers. Alternatively keep `available_memory = num_blocks * native_pool_bytes_per_block` in AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder.get_kv_cache_config_from_groups, but only if it is never re-overridden and each model planner's divisor exactly equals native_pool_bytes_per_block. Also update AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder.get_kv_cache_config_from_groups (line 168) to stop passing `num_blocks * bytes_per_block` if the helper is converted to num_blocks.

Third issue: _pool_bytes_per_block_from_builder no longer temporarily clears num_gpu_blocks_override around its `num_blocks=1` probe. AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder._get_pool_bytes_per_block (line 182) probes via get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(..., num_blocks=1); if any internal may_override remains, the probe is resized to num_gpu_blocks_override and the per-block byte cost (used for override accounting, check_memory, auto-fit and rank re-planning) becomes wrong. Remove all internal override application so the probe stays at one block.

Fourth: KVCacheGroup.max_memory_usage_bytes is removed in vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py. vllm-ascend currently appears to use only KVCacheSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes (which remains), but any group-level caller must switch to max_allocated_blocks_per_request(vllm_config) * page_size_bytes or to planning._max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups. Likewise max_memory_usage_bytes, estimate_max_model_len, check_enough_kv_cache_memory, get_uniform_page_size and is_kv_cache_type_attention_free are deleted from kv_cache_planning; production vllm-ascend does not import them, but any local helper/test using them must migrate to the surviving _check_enough_kv_cache_memory(builder, vllm_config, groups, available_memory) / _max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups / _estimate_max_model_len_from_groups.

Tests: update direct module-level calls that still pass available_memory= (e.g. tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/test_mooncake_connector.py:413) to num_blocks=; replace monkeypatch targets of vllm_ascend.core.kv_cache_config_builder.may_override_num_blocks in tests/ut/worker/test_attn_utils_v2.py and tests/ut/patch/platform/test_prefix_cache_cp_patches.py; and rewrite model-plan tests that pass available_memory to _get_kv_cache_config_deepseek_v4_main / paired_sfa_cache_config / get_glm5_next_kv_cache_config / get_qwen4_exp_kv_cache_config / get_deepseek_v41_kv_cache_config / get_step5_kv_cache_config_from_groups / tq_cache.cache_config while asserting num_gpu_blocks_override behavior (test_deepseek_v41_cache.py:496, test_glm5next_cache_config.py, test_qwen4_exp_cache_config.py, test_step5_cache_config.py:275, test_turboquant/test_capacity.py, test_paired_sfa_cache.py, test_hisparse_admission.py). If vllm-ascend still supports older vLLM lanes, guard the may_override import/behavior with vllm_version_is and provide a local fallback helper.
deep_analysis.risk: High. Missing the import fix breaks vllm-ascend at import time for all NPU startup. Misinterpreting byte budgets as block counts after the get_kv_cache_config_from_groups signature change can silently produce enormous or zero block counts, causing OOM, capacity mismatch, or inconsistent num_blocks across PP/TP ranks. Removing/retaining may_override_num_blocks incorrectly changes num_gpu_blocks_override semantics and the one-block pool-cost probe used for auto-fit, admission and layerwise reuse, which is especially risky for the Ascend custom layouts (DeepSeek-V4.1/V4, GLM-Next, Qwen4-Exp, Kimi-K3 paired SFA, Step5, TurboQuant, HiSparse/DSpark) where each planner has its own divisor and aliasing geometry. The change also touches many unit tests and cross-rank convergence paths, so it needs broad NPU KV-cache sizing and multi-rank regression testing.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: 1) vllm_ascend/ec_manager/score_ec_manager.py: update ScoreEncoderCacheManager.create_manager() (line ~104) to set manager.enable_events from vllm_config.ec_events_config.enable_ec_cache_events (the base create_manager does this, but Score overrides it and currently skips it). Override try_rollback_allocations(): the inherited base implementation mutates the one-tier state (self.freeable/self.num_embeds_by_hash/self.freed), which ScoreEncoderCacheManager never populates (it uses npu_freeable/cpu_freeable, npu_cache/cpu_cache and manager metadata), so the new upstream PRIORITY-preemption call can raise KeyError. Implement rollback for both NPU and CPU tiers, remove queued ECStored events, and emit ECRemoved as appropriate. Add _record_event(ECStored/ECRemoved) in allocate(), check_and_update_cache()/promotion, can_allocate() CPU eviction, evict_from_npu(), and free_encoder_input(); update reset()/the reset path to clear self.events and record AllECCleared. 2) Mirror the new Scheduler behaviour in the three copied schedule() implementations: vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py BalanceScheduler.schedule (~169/869), vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py RecomputeScheduler.schedule (~203/992), and vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py DyntraLBScheduler.schedule (~405/1184). Pass encoder_cache_events=self.encoder_cache_manager.take_events() or None and encoder_cache_epoch=self._encoder_cache_epoch into SchedulerOutput/RecomputeSchedulerOutput, and copy the new PRIORITY-preemption branch that calls encoder_cache_manager.try_rollback_allocations() and only removes scheduled_encoder_inputs after the rollback decision. 3) Guard all EC-event field/import use with vllm_version_is() because ECEventsConfig, ec_events_config, SchedulerOutput.encoder_cache_events/encoder_cache_epoch and try_rollback_allocations do not exist on the supported vLLM 0.34.0 lane. 4) Optionally implement ECConnectorBase.take_events() in Ascend EC connectors that own off-device encoder outputs (memcache/mooncake/cpu); the inherited default returning () is safe but suppresses connector-originated events. The scheduler-created ec_event_publisher is inherited correctly because all Ascend scheduler __init__ paths call super().__init__, so no change is needed in vllm_ascend/platform.py or config patches. 5) Update Ascend unit tests that use MagicMock ec_connector: set take_events.return_value=() before calling update_from_output, matching the upstream test change.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. The feature is opt-in and defaults off, so normal Ascend serving is mostly unaffected; however the new try_rollback_allocations() call runs regardless of event enablement under PRIORITY scheduling with scheduled encoder inputs, and ScoreEncoderCacheManager's inherited implementation is incompatible with its two-tier state (likely KeyError on self.freeable.pop), so a priority-preemption multimodal workload could crash. The three copied Ascend schedulers silently omit encoder_cache_events/epoch and the new rollback path, so EC events are lost and preemption behaviour diverges from upstream when those schedulers are active. Adding fields/imports without vllm_version_is guards will break the 0.34.0 lane, and tests mocking ec_connector may fail until take_events is stubbed.

vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler.Scheduler.should_schedule / _idle_step / skip_idle_steps / _has_decode_awaiting_cadence / _needs_no_more_steps, consumed indirectly by all Ascend Scheduler subclasses

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
1) Update the three copied/forked schedule() implementations to track the new PP idle-step and microbatch-cap semantics (vLLM commit 249e65290922).
- vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py::RecomputeScheduler.schedule: after the `if self._pause_state == PauseState.PAUSED_ALL: token_budget = 0` block, add `if self.pp_microbatch_cap is not None and token_budget > 0: token_budget = self.pp_microbatch_cap.apply(token_budget)`. After `self._update_after_schedule(scheduler_output)` and before `return scheduler_output`, add `if self.skip_idle_steps and not total_num_scheduled_tokens and not self._has_decode_awaiting_cadence(): self._idle_step = scheduler_output`. Also replace the hand-inlined `num_output_placeholders` / `num_computed_tokens + 2` guards (around line 271) with `self._needs_no_more_steps(request)` where available (keep the old expression under a version guard for 0.34.0).
- vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py::DyntraLBScheduler.schedule: same three changes (budget apply near lines 435-437, idle-step marking near lines 1232-1236, `_needs_no_more_steps` near line 468).
- vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py::BalanceScheduler.schedule enabled path: apply `self.pp_microbatch_cap.apply(token_budget)` after the PAUSED_ALL branch (near lines 198-201) and the guarded `_idle_step` assignment after `_update_after_schedule` (near lines 911-912). The disabled path already calls `super().schedule(throttle_prefills)` so it inherits the new behavior; update the file docstring which claims the copied schedule retains upstream behavior.
Use version/feature guards: these are copied across vLLM 0.34.0 and main, so gate with `vllm_version_is("0.34.0")` or `getattr(self, 'pp_microbatch_cap', None)` / `getattr(self, 'skip_idle_steps', False)` / `hasattr(self, '_needs_no_more_steps')` to avoid AttributeError on the older supported vLLM.

2) Preserve the upstream DP guard. `skip_idle_steps` and EngineCore `_pp_admission` are true only for `pipeline_parallel_size > 1 and data_parallel_size == 1`. Do not apply `_idle_step` bookkeeping in DP-only configurations (BalanceScheduler enabled path, DyntraLB DP) beyond what the base class already sets; the DP busy loop intentionally runs a dummy batch on idle steps. `PPMicrobatchCap.create` already returns None when pp_size == 1, so the cap can be applied even on PP+DP copies.

3) Verify the KV-cache probing path. `KVCacheManager.__init__` now builds `prefix_probe_group_ids` from `coordinator.single_type_managers` using `manager.kv_cache_group_id`, `manager.block_size` and `isinstance(manager, FullAttentionManager)`, and `extend_cached_prefix` calls `block_pool.get_cached_block(hash, group_ids)` with `request.block_hashes`. AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator does expose `single_type_managers`, and KpoolTailManager subclasses FullAttentionManager, so this should work, but confirm for every Ascend KV cache flavor (HISPARSE_SOURCE fallback to upstream coordinator, GLM kpool tail, DeepSeek V4 nested specs, DCP/PCP worlds) that the relevant full-attention manager is included and that hash_block_size equals manager.block_size. If not, extend_cached_prefix silently returns the unextended prefix and the PP cap overestimates the prefill backlog (perf-only, not correctness); add an Ascend override/test if accurate sizing matters. Ensure custom waiting queues (ShortRequestFirstRequestQueue, BatchJobAwareRequestQueue) stay iterable because PPMicrobatchCap.apply iterates `kv_holding_waiting`, `waiting`, and `async_kv_waiting`.

4) Engine core: vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_engine_core.py and the DP subclasses (BalanceDPEngineCoreProc, DyntraLBDPEngineCoreProc) only override `run_engine_core`, `_has_global_unfinished_reqs`, `_init_data_parallel`, `add_request`, so they are not broken by the `EngineCoreProc._wait_for_output` -> `_handle_inputs_while_waiting` rename. Still verify no Ascend out-of-tree subclass overrides `_wait_for_output`; if one does, rename it to `_handle_inputs_while_waiting(self, future, stop_on_add=False)` and return bool. For any Ascend PP-specific engine core, mirror `_wait_for_new_request` / `_pp_admission` and the new `scheduler.should_schedule()` gating in `step_with_batch_queue`.

5) Config propagation/tests. RecomputeSchedulerConfig.initialize_from_config copies all `field.init` fields, so `pp_microbatch_min_tokens` is inherited automatically; no explicit change needed unless a field allow/deny list is added. Add Ascend unit tests for: should_schedule() returning False after an idle empty step and True after add_request/update_from_output; PP microbatch cap chunk sizes for RecomputeScheduler/DyntraLBScheduler/BalanceScheduler; PP+async admission of a new request past an idle empty step; and cap being None for non-chunked prefill / mamba-block-aligned splits. Consider exposing/validating `--pp-microbatch-min-tokens` in Ascend CLI/docs if PP is a supported deployment surface.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. There is no hard import/ABC break: should_schedule is non-abstract, SchedulerConfig/EngineArgs additions are additive, and the Ascend coordinator exposes single_type_managers. The main risk is silent behavioral divergence: RecomputeScheduler, DyntraLBScheduler and the BalanceScheduler enabled path fork Scheduler.schedule and will not set _idle_step or apply PPMicrobatchCap, so Ascend PP/PP+async deployments lose the new admission/latency behavior (new requests cannot be admitted past an in-flight idle empty step) and prefill microbatches are not sized from the backlog. This is a perf/latency regression relative to upstream, and the divergence is easy to miss because upstream unit tests exercise only the base Scheduler. A second risk is applying the new idle-step logic in DP configurations where data_parallel_size > 1, which would conflict with the DP busy-loop dummy-batch behavior and could cause extra empty steps or stalls; the skip_idle_steps/_pp_admission guards must be preserved. Third, the PP cap's prefix probing depends on Ascend-specific KV layouts (Mamba align, HISPARSE, kpool tail, DCP/PCP, offload/KVPP); an incorrect hit estimate only changes chunk sizes but should still be validated against need_mamba_block_aligned_split and num_prefill_lookahead to avoid zero-token or overly small steps. Version-guarding is required because vllm-ascend still supports vLLM 0.34.0, where these new attributes do not exist.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
No hard break: enable_logging_iteration_details is off by default; the new IterationDetails/SchedulerStats fields are appended with None defaults, create_request_queue's new tally arg is optional, and all Ascend schedulers call super().__init__ so self.queued_workload_tally always exists (no AttributeError). Adaptation is needed for the new opt-in workload-snapshot metrics to be correct/complete in Ascend fork modes:
1) In the three verbatim copies of Scheduler.schedule() — vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py (line ~950 block setting num_encoder_output_tokens), vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py (~1128), vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py (~827) — import make_scheduled_workload from vllm.v1.metrics.iteration_workload and, inside the existing `if iteration_details is not None:` block, add `if self.observability_config.enable_logging_iteration_details: iteration_details.scheduled_workload = make_scheduled_workload(scheduled_new_reqs, scheduled_running_reqs, num_scheduled_tokens)`. The variables are already in scope in each copy.
2) Custom waiting queues bypass the tally: vllm_ascend/core/batch_job_aware_scheduler.py replaces self.waiting with BatchJobAwareRequestQueue, and vllm_ascend/core/short_request_first_scheduler.py::install_short_request_first_waiting_queue replaces self.waiting with ShortRequestFirstRequestQueue (its internal lanes are built with create_request_queue without a tally). To keep SchedulerStats.queued_workload accurate, either wrap these with TalliedRequestQueue when scheduler.queued_workload_tally is not None, or have their add/pop/prepend/remove paths call tally.add/tally.discard.
3) Where Ascend overrides schedule/update paths that mutate request.status or request.num_computed_tokens while the request stays queued (e.g. RecomputeScheduler.update_from_output / _preempt_or_recompute, DyntraLBScheduler._preempt_request / _free_request), mirror the upstream calls to self._refresh_queued_workload(request) so the tally stays consistent.
4) Add/extend unit tests analogous to tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py to assert scheduled_workload and queued_workload for each Ascend scheduler mode when --enable-logging-iteration-details is set.
deep_analysis.risk: Low. The change is observability-only and guarded by enable_logging_iteration_details (default off); the default Ascend path (upstream Scheduler) inherits the feature and all new fields are optional, so there is no crash or behavior regression. The main risk is silent metric incompleteness/inaccuracy under Ascend's forked schedulers and custom request queues if not synced, plus a small risk of tally drift if in-place request state changes in the copied schedule() paths are not mirrored; no impact on scheduling decisions, KV allocation, or model execution.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
The commit is a true positive: it reuses the same cache_config.use_replayssm flag that vllm-ascend uses to select its Qwen GDN RecoverSSM path, but it now enables upstream GDN standard-decode ReplaySSM inside QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention and advertises SupportsReplaySSM on Qwen3.5/Qwen4Exp.

1) vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_qwen3_5.py (highest priority): the wrapper _gdn_init_with_packed_weight calls the upstream QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.__init__, which after this commit sets self.use_replayssm = cache_config.use_replayssm and raises ValueError through _replayssm_unsupported_reason when num_speculative_tokens > 0. Ascend's GDN RecoverSSM always requires spec decode and leaves use_replayssm=True, so model construction will now fail. Prevent the upstream branch from arming for Ascend GDN: either temporarily set vllm_config.cache_config.use_replayssm=False while calling _GDN_ORIGINAL_INIT and restore it afterwards, or patch QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention._replayssm_unsupported_reason/__init__ so it does not raise; then force self.use_replayssm=False, self.replayssm_buffer_len=None, self._plans_replayssm_decode=False, leave _replayssm_ring_start/_replayssm_prev_num_accepted empty, and keep the existing use_gdn_recoverssm/AscendGDNRecoverSSMAttentionBackend selection unchanged. This also keeps upstream initialize_replayssm_ring_trackers/get_replayssm_block_copy_tensors from treating GDN as a ReplaySSM layer.

2) vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_replayssm_config.py::validate_mamba_cached_kernel: is_gdn_model currently excludes Qwen4Exp, and validate_qwen_gdn_recoverssm requires num_spec > 0. After this commit Qwen3.5/Qwen4Exp report supports_replayssm=True, so for Qwen4Exp (and any GDN standard-decode use_replayssm with num_spec==0) the wrapper falls through to the upstream validator, which now accepts upstream GDN ring support that Ascend does not implement. Add an explicit Ascend guard: detect GDN/Qwen4Exp and either reject --use-replayssm standard decode with a clear ValueError or clear/neutralize the flag before calling the original validator. Keep the existing early return for Ascend GDN spec RecoverSSM.

3) vllm_ascend/models/qwen_gdn_recoverssm.py: the new MambaStateDtypeCalculator.gated_delta_net_state_dtype(..., use_replayssm=False) and MambaStateShapeCalculator.gated_delta_net_state_shape(..., replayssm_buffer_len=None) are backward compatible, but make the Ascend helpers explicitly pass use_replayssm=False/replayssm_buffer_len=None (or assert use_replayssm is not honored) so the new (d,k,g) ReplaySSM rings are never appended on top of Ascend's single RecoverSSM replay record. Keep the extra (local_v_heads, num_spec+1, head_v_dim+head_k_dim+1) record. Update _GDN_MODEL_TYPES/_GDN_ARCHITECTURES if Qwen4Exp is to be covered.

4) vllm_ascend/attention/gdn.py: AscendGatedDeltaNetAttention.get_state_shape/get_state_dtype must keep returning the Ascend layouts (conv, ssm, optional recoverssm record) independent of cache_config.use_replayssm/self.use_replayssm; do not echo the upstream 5-tuple. If upstream GDN ReplaySSM is ever adopted on NPU, instead implement the 5-state kv_cache unpack (conv, ssm, d_cache, k_cache, g_cache), pass replayssm_buffer_len into the shape calculator, add an Ascend _replayssm_decode equivalent using get_replayssm_config('gdn_decode')/plan_replayssm_decode, and honor the new GDNAttentionMetadata write_pos_d/is_flush_d/replayssm_seq_lens_d/replayssm_align_block_size fields. Until then ensure the upstream _forward_core_packed ReplaySSM branch is unreachable on Ascend.

5) vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/model.py: AscendQwen4ExpForCausalLM.get_gdn_mamba_state_shape_from_config delegates to the upstream classmethod, which now appends ReplaySSM rings when use_replayssm is set; AscendQwen4ExpForCausalLM.get_mamba_specs_from_config filters specs by len(spec.shapes) == 2 and will silently drop the GDN state spec if 5 shapes are returned. Either reject --use-replayssm for Qwen4Exp in step 2 or make this override force the 2-state layout (and filter by mamba_type/layer rather than tuple length). Update MambaStateShapes return annotations.

6) vllm_ascend/_310p/...: _310p_get_state_dtype destructures only the first two entries of GatedDeltaNetAttention.get_state_dtype, which still returns a 2-tuple, so it is safe, but confirm the 310P patch still overrides QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.get_state_dtype/get_state_shape and add a 310P rejection for Qwen4Exp/Qwen3.5 standard-decode --use-replayssm (currently the GDN check only covers _GDN_MODEL_TYPES).

7) Update tests: extend tests/ut/models/test_qwen_gdn_recoverssm_config.py (shape/dtype counts for the new optional parameters), add regressions that QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.__init__ succeeds for Ascend GDN RecoverSSM with use_replayssm + spec decode, and that GDN/Qwen4Exp standard-decode --use-replayssm is rejected or disabled on Ascend. Add a metadata-builder test asserting write_pos_d/is_flush_d stay None on Ascend's RecoverSSM path.
deep_analysis.risk: High if unadapted: the new unconditional QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.__init__ validation raises 'GDN ReplaySSM does not support speculative decoding yet' whenever cache_config.use_replayssm is set with num_spec>0, which is exactly how vllm-ascend selects its Qwen GDN RecoverSSM today, so all Qwen3.5/Qwen3-Next RecoverSSM serving would fail at model construction. A second, subtler risk is silent KV-cache layout corruption: adding SupportsReplaySSM to Qwen3.5/Qwen4Exp makes upstream validation accept standard-decode --use-replayssm, and the upstream shape/dtype calculators then return 5 states while Ascend layers still read kv_cache[0]/[1]; this can produce wrong state pages, wrong outputs, or crashes instead of a config error. Qwen4Exp's get_mamba_specs_from_config filter of len(shapes)==2 can also drop the GDN spec entirely. The upstream Mamba2-only gating in mamba_attn.py and the gcd(block_size, prefix_match_unit) align change are low risk for Ascend because Ascend has no Mamba2 ReplaySSM path, but any future Mamba2 support must mirror them.

affected_interfaces: vllm_ascend.patch.platform.patch_kv_cache_coordinator.AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit / find_longest_cache_hit_per_group (pcp_world_size kwarg forwarded to upstream manager_cls.find_longest_cache_hit)

vllm-ascend unit tests constructing KV cache managers/coordinators with pcp_world_size (test_prefix_cache_cp_patches.py, test_compressed_prefix_cache.py, test_mamba_prefix_admission.py, test_patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py, test_preempt_offload_connector.py, distributed/ascend_store/_mock_deps.py)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: Remove all remaining pcp_world_size plumbing that vllm-ascend passes into the upstream KV-cache APIs; the parameter no longer exists on KVCacheManager, KVCacheCoordinator subclasses, get_kv_cache_coordinator, SingleTypeKVCacheManager and every find_longest_cache_hit override. Concretely: (1) vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py - drop pcp_world_size from AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator.__init__ and remove `del pcp_world_size`; remove `pcp_world_size=1` from the get_manager_for_kv_cache_spec(...) manager construction (~line 191), from both manager_cls.find_longest_cache_hit(...) calls in find_longest_cache_hit and find_longest_cache_hit_per_group (~lines 447/509), and from the patched get_kv_cache_coordinator signature plus hybrid_kwargs/orig_kwargs (~lines 525/545/587). Forwarding pcp_world_size into _orig_get_kv_cache_coordinator or the manager constructor will raise TypeError at coordinator creation. (2) vllm_ascend/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py - remove the pcp_world_size parameter from AscendCircularBufferManager.__init__ and the corresponding positional argument in super().__init__; otherwise the removed slot shifts needs_kv_cache_zeroing/max_admission_blocks_per_request and can silently disable/enable KV zeroing or corrupt retention/admission settings. While there, verify the upstream constructor's first argument (now kv_cache_group in the synced vLLM main, via the separate create_single_type_manager change) matches this subclass. (3) vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_mamba_manager.py - remove pcp_world_size from AscendMambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit and stop forwarding it to super(); keep dcp_world_size=1 override. (4) vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/kv_offload/preempt_offload/manager.py - remove `pcp_world_size=1` from the get_kv_cache_coordinator(...) call (~line 114). (5) vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/kv_cache.py - remove the now-unused pcp_world_size argument from KpoolTailManager.find_longest_cache_hit (harmless but keeps the override aligned). (6) Update affected UTs: remove pcp_world_size kwargs/constructors and the `manager.pcp_world_size` assertion in tests/ut/patch/platform/test_prefix_cache_cp_patches.py, remove `coordinator.call_args.kwargs["pcp_world_size"]` assertion in tests/ut/kv_offload/test_preempt_offload_connector.py, and update tests/ut/test_compressed_prefix_cache.py, tests/ut/patch/platform/test_mamba_prefix_admission.py, tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py and tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/_mock_deps.py. PCP worker/attention code (vllm_ascend/worker/v2/pcp_manager.py, attention/context_parallel/*) reads parallel_config or its own _pcp_world_size and needs no change.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. Missing a call site causes an immediate TypeError at engine startup or at the first prefix-cache lookup: the patched coordinator delegates pcp_world_size into upstream get_kv_cache_coordinator, upstream manager constructors, or MambaManager.find_longest_cache_hit. The AscendCircularBufferManager positional super() call is the highest-risk spot because leaving the stale argument does not necessarily crash; it can shift needs_kv_cache_zeroing/max_admission_blocks_per_request and silently alter KV-cache zeroing or admission/retention behavior. Test coverage currently asserts the removed pcp_world_size attribute and would fail until updated. No model/accuracy change is expected once adapted.

affected_interfaces: vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils.resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes (semantics change: raises ValueError when an explicit cache_config.prefix_match_unit would fall back to scheduler_block_size)
vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager.SingleTypeKVCacheManager.supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup (now consulted at startup; SlidingWindowManager and CircularBufferManager are False)
vllm_ascend.models.glm5next.kv_cache.KpoolTailManager (sets supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup=False but inherits manager-level prefix_cacheable=True from FullAttentionManager)

vllm_ascend.patch.platform.patch_kv_cache_coordinator.AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator (enable_partial_hash_hits, _cache_hit_alignment_tokens, find_longest_cache_hit mirror the upstream fine-grained/fallback logic)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: 1) In vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/kv_cache.py, make KpoolTailManager agree with AscendIndexerKPoolTailSpec.prefix_cacheable=False, e.g. add `@classmethod def prefix_cacheable(cls, config): return False`. Without this, KVCacheGroup.prefix_cacheable is True (inherited from FullAttentionManager), so upstream _unsupported_fine_grained_managers sees a prefix-cacheable manager with supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup=False and block_size (=compress_ratio) != hash_block_size and raises ValueError for an explicit --prefix-match-unit (previously a silent fallback). It also incorrectly pulls the private tail block size into hashing_sizes/divisibility checks. 2) Audit all Ascend custom managers/specs (vllm_ascend/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py::AscendCircularBufferManager, Kimi-K3/SFA, Step5, Qwen4-Exp, DSpark, and AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec users) so manager-level prefix_cacheable and supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup match the spec: set supports=True only when find_longest_cache_hit genuinely accepts alignment_tokens < block_size; sliding-window/circular managers must stay False. 3) Reconcile vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py (AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator.enable_partial_hash_hits, _cache_hit_alignment_tokens, find_longest_cache_hit, tail_pool_alignment) with upstream resolve_cache_hit_alignment_tokens and the new _unsupported_fine_grained_managers so startup validation and runtime alignment cannot diverge. Upstream now refuses the fallback, so remove/avoid any Ascend path that assumes a silent downgrade; if a specific layout must keep the old behavior, patch/clamp CacheConfig.prefix_match_unit instead of relying on the coordinator. 4) Update tests that set an explicit prefix_match_unit on hybrid layouts: tests/ut/patch/platform/test_prefix_cache_cp_patches.py (test_glm5_next_hashes_exclude_private_tail_after_engine_min_block_update with unit 8/32, test_real_tail_coordinator_preserves_prefix_hit_and_private_lifecycle with unit 16, DCP reject tests), tests/ut/kv_offload/test_hybrid_prefix_truncation.py, tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/*, tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/test_scheduler_integration.py, and e2e tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_qwen3_5_0_8b.py::test_hybrid_prefix_match_unit_cached_output_consistency. Assert either successful startup with a block-aligned unit or the new ValueError naming the offending manager. 5) Ensure connector paths do not assume leniency: when kv_transfer_config is set, upstream still raises for unsupported managers (KpoolTail/SWA), although the plain 'hits land on scheduler block size' error is suppressed. Add a real-engine (LLM/vllm serve path) regression for GLM5Next and DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 with enable_prefix_caching + explicit prefix_match_unit. 6) Update Ascend user docs/CLI guidance: prefix_match_unit must equal the block size for groups requiring block-aligned lookups (sliding-window attention), must be compatible with sparse-MLA per-state compression, and may now be rejected for GLM-Next's private tail.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. The change is startup-time fail-fast in common core code that vllm-ascend calls directly, and the failure occurs before engine initialization, so existing user scripts serving GLM-Next or DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 hybrid models with --prefix-match-unit can start failing. The main correctness pitfalls are (a) manager-level vs spec-level prefix cacheability divergence in Ascend custom managers (especially KpoolTailManager), which can both trigger spurious ValueErrors and change hash granularity, and (b) divergence between upstream startup validation and AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator's runtime enable_partial_hash_hits/_cache_hit_alignment_tokens. Connector-enabled configurations (Mooncake/AscendStore/offload) do not bypass the unsupported-manager error, so KV-transfer tests and deployments need explicit coverage. Several existing UT/e2e tests encode the old silent-fallback behavior and will fail until updated.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
Root cause: upstream vLLM main is now pinned to torch==2.14 (requirements/cuda.txt) and this commit deletes all torch<=2.12 workarounds, while vllm-ascend still pins torch==2.10.0 / torch-npu==2.10.0.post7 (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, mkdocs.yml). Two viable paths:

(A) Preferred: raise the Ascend torch/torch-npu baseline to >=2.12 (update requirements.txt, pyproject.toml build deps, mkdocs.yml release_pytorch_version, Dockerfile/Dockerfile.a3/Dockerfile.a5/Dockerfile.310p and CI images), then re-validate CANN 9.x/triton-ascend kernels. Once torch>=2.12 the deleted guards are valid.

(B) If torch-npu 2.12 is not available, vendor the deleted compatibility layer in vllm-ascend:
1. vllm_ascend/__init__.py (before importing anything from vllm): on torch<2.11 create sys.modules['torch._opaque_base'] with OpaqueBase=object and stub torch._library.opaque_object.register_opaque_type if absent, mirroring the existing triton stub pattern. Also force VLLM_USE_LAYERNAME=0 (or patch vllm.utils.torch_utils._USE_LAYERNAME=False) so LayerName strings are not used as opaque types on torch 2.10.
2. Add vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_compilation.py imported from patch/platform/__init__.py: wrap vllm.compilation.backends.split_graph (or torch.fx.passes.split_module.split_module) to drop tuple_return=True when torch<2.12; otherwise VllmBackend piecewise splitting raises TypeError before AscendCompiler is invoked.
3. Add vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_env_override_compat.py re-implementing the removed torch-2.10 backports that Ascend's compile path needs: FxGraphCachePickler.dumps ValueError->BypassFxGraphCache (torch 2.10.x), GraphCaptureOutput.get_runtime_env builtins/external_refs fix (torch 2.10-2.11), OperatorIssue.operator_str short-circuit (torch<2.13), and pattern_matcher.fallback_node_due_to_unsupported_type backport (torch<2.16). Do not re-add 2.11-only patches (cpp indirect_assert, constrain_to_fx_strides) on 2.10.
4. Patch vllm.compilation.decorators._support_torch_compile to omit mark_unbacked(shape_id=/hint_override=) when torch<2.11, and guard the unconditional inductor config assume_32bit_indexing for torch<2.10. Ascend currently passes int dynamic_arg_dims, so this is defensive but needed for any upstream model.
5. Extend vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_torch_accelerator.py to map torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache to a torch.npu implementation or no-op, because cleanup_dist_env_and_memory now calls it without the old AttributeError/version guard.
6. Re-check vllm.config.vllm's forced fast_moe_cold_start=False and envs.use_mega_aot_artifact now defaulting to 1; Ascend does not currently read these, but confirm no Ascend path relies on fast_moe_cold_start or the InductorStandaloneAdaptor/MEGA_AOT path.
7. Add regression coverage: import smoke test on torch 2.10 (engine init, AscendCompiler VLLM_COMPILE graph split), and a compile/replay test exercising split_graph plus npugraph_ex/torchair.
deep_analysis.risk: High. On torch 2.10 the new vllm.utils.torch_utils module-level import of torch._opaque_base (and register_opaque_type) fails immediately, which breaks importing essentially all of vllm_ascend (direct_register_custom_op consumers, fused MoE _encode_layer_name, patch modules). Independently, VllmBackend.split_graph now always passes tuple_return=True to torch.fx split_module, which does not exist before torch 2.12, so every VLLM_COMPILE piecewise split fails before AscendCompiler runs. Removing the env_override torch 2.10-2.13 backports can also reintroduce Inductor/FxGraphCache/AOT-cache compile failures and compile-time hangs. Bumping torch/torch-npu instead carries broad CANN/operator compatibility risk across all Ascend hardware profiles (A2/A3/A5/310P).
